title: Religions Around the World
objective: After this level you can describe the world's major religions and where they are practiced.
summary: Christians are about 29% of the world, Muslims 26%, the unaffiliated 24%. Most Muslims, Hindus and Buddhists live in Asia-Pacific; sub-Saharan Africa now has the most Christians.

cards.headline: The world's largest religion now has more followers in Africa than in Europe.
cards.body: If you picture Christianity centered on Europe, your map needs an update. Religion has a geography, and that geography moves.

cards.headline: The big picture
cards.body: No single religion claims a majority of humanity. Christians are the largest group: about 2.3 billion people, or about 29% of the world in 2020. Muslims follow at about 26%. Third place is a surprise: people with no religion at all, about 24%. Hindus make up about 15% and Buddhists about 4%. Roughly one in four people on Earth checks the 'none' box.

cards.headline: Faith follows people
cards.body: Level 91 put about 60% of humanity in the Asia-Pacific region. Religion tracks that crowd. About 59% of Muslims live in Asia-Pacific, so most Muslims live east of the Middle East, not in it. For Hindus the share is 99%, and for Buddhists 98%. Two of the world's big religions are almost entirely Asian.

mascot.line: Picture a 'typical' Muslim and you might picture the Middle East. The numbers point further east.

cards.headline: On the move
cards.body: Religious maps change. By 2020, sub-Saharan Africa had overtaken Europe as the region with the most Christians, home to about 31% of them. Meanwhile, from 2010 to 2020, Muslims were the fastest-growing major group, and people with no religion also grew as a share of the world. A religious map, like a city ranking, needs a date on it.

cards.headline: Religions: placed
learned: Most Muslims, Hindus and Buddhists live in Asia-Pacific
Sub-Saharan Africa now has the most Christians

questions.prompt: Which region is home to the largest number of Christians today?

options.label: Europe
options.rationale: It held that title until sub-Saharan Africa overtook it.

options.label: North America
options.rationale: Far fewer than the leading region.

options.label: The Middle East
options.rationale: Christianity began there, but it's now a small share.

questions.explanation: By 2020, sub-Saharan Africa had overtaken Europe, with about 31% of the world's Christians.

questions.prompt: People with no religion are about 24% of the world. Where does that put them among the largest groups?

options.label: Second, ahead of Muslims
options.rationale: Muslims, at about 26%, are slightly larger.

questions.explanation: Christians (about 29%) and Muslims (about 26%) are larger; the unaffiliated come third at about 24%, ahead of Hindus and Buddhists.

questions.prompt: Most Muslims, and nearly all Hindus and Buddhists, live in one region. Which Level 91 region is it?

options.label: Sub-Saharan Africa
options.rationale: It has the most Christians, not most followers of these three.

options.label: Europe
options.rationale: Only a small share of these groups live there.

options.label: The Middle East
options.rationale: Most Muslims live east of it.

questions.explanation: About 59% of Muslims, 99% of Hindus and 98% of Buddhists live in Asia-Pacific, home to about 60% of all people.
